claims.statement: The scheduler graph is a single-node StateGraph (START -> launch -> END) registered as the `scheduler` assistant in langgraph.json, and its `_launch` node deterministically routes each tick without invoking an LLM.

The scheduler routes `reconcile`, `baby_sit`, `background_tasks`, `session_cost`, `thread_feedback`, and `agent_cost` tasks to their bounded handlers; it also supports expedited-review and workspace-refresh task constants, and otherwise launches a stored scheduled-agent run.

When a scheduler tick is missing its required key (watch_key, thread_id, or schedule_id), `_launch` returns a `missing_*` status result instead of raising, so a malformed tick degrades to a no-op rather than crashing the cron.

Dashboard-managed recurring agent schedules validate cron strings with normalize_cron_schedule, which requires a five-field expression and range-checks each field (supporting steps, ranges, and lists) before a schedule is stored.

launch_scheduled_agent_run loads a stored schedule record, only launches records whose trigger is `schedule`, and delegates a matching record to the schedule launch path; schedule run state is stored separately from the definition.

reconcile_stale_runs is the durable-dispatch safety net: it paginates every `busy` thread, lists its `pending` runs, and cancels (action=interrupt) those older than max_age_seconds (default 1800s), so runs whose completion webhook never fired do not hold a thread busy forever.
The reconcile sweep wraps per-thread work in try/except so one bad thread never aborts the sweep, and returns counts of threads checked, stale runs found, and runs cancelled.

Session-cost refresh is a self-terminating chain of stateless delayed scheduler runs: a refresh performs one Slack-footer update attempt and enqueues the next attempt only on a transient `pending` result, following a fixed five-delay list.

Each baby-sit watch is a BabySitWatch persisted in the `baby_sit_watches` store keyed by lower-cased owner/repo#pr_number, binding the watch to the originating agent thread_id, head SHA/ref, GitHub App installation id, captured run_config, and a SourceContext.

A pull request may be watched from only one agent thread at a time: start_watch rejects a second thread that tries to watch an already-active PR, and carries over retry/dedupe state only when the head SHA is unchanged.

start_watch registers each watch's per-watch LangGraph cron via _ensure_watch_cron, which idempotently reuses an existing cron tagged kind=baby_sit_watch (deleting duplicates) or creates one, and rolls back the store row and partial cron if cron creation fails for a brand-new watch.

The per-watch baby_sit cron fires on the fixed */10 * * * * schedule against the scheduler assistant, providing a deterministic 10-minute fallback that dispatches no agent run for pending, settling, or duplicate CI state.

Signed GitHub CI webhooks trigger immediate watch evaluation: the webhook route verifies the X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC before processing, and handle_ci_webhook ignores non-failing payloads, matches active watches by head SHA or branch, and de-duplicates by webhook delivery_id.
Both the webhook trigger and the cron trigger funnel into watch evaluation under a per-key short-lived lock thread, so at most one evaluation of a given watch runs at a time.

On a new head SHA evaluation resets retry_count, settle state, and dedupe key lists; on a genuinely new failing state it dispatches a baby-sit continuation to the originating agent thread, skipping dispatch when the per-head failure fingerprint was already dispatched.
Baby-sit signals success only after the exact check set has been stable for CHECK_SET_SETTLE_MINUTES (10 minutes), avoiding a premature green while checks are still being added.

Flaky reruns are capped per head SHA at MAX_RETRIES_PER_HEAD (3), and record_retry increments the durable retry count (rejecting the call when the head changed or the cap is reached) while posting the flaky-CI alert only on the first occurrence of a given check and safe URL for that head via alert_keys dedupe.

Terminal watch outcomes (PR closed/merged, settled success, terminal non-rerunnable checks needing triage, flaky-rerun cap reached, or MAX_EVALUATION_ERRORS consecutive evaluation failures) are notified through SourceContext when possible and otherwise fall back to a /baby-sit --terminal run on the originating agent thread, then the watch is stopped.

The manage_baby_sit tool is the agent-facing surface for durable watches, requiring canonical PR URLs and an executable thread; start verifies GitHub authentication, open-PR head data, and App installation, while stop and record_retry enforce current-thread watch ownership.

background_tasks provides model-free monitoring: ensure_background_task_cron idempotently registers a kind=background_tasks cron on the every-minute (* * * * *) schedule bound to a thread, and monitor_background_tasks claims each terminal task atomically, dispatches a completion message to the originating thread, and deletes its own cron once no task is running or pending so monitoring self-terminates.

schedule_thread_wakeup schedules a one-shot re-trigger of the current agent thread (1 minute to 24 hours) as a single-fire cron against the `agent` assistant carrying an end_time about 90 seconds past the fire so it never re-fires, and passes through selected config keys with a default polling prompt.

Thread wakeups are budget-limited to at most _MAX_WAKEUPS_BETWEEN_USER_MESSAGES (10) between human messages, keyed to the latest human-message generation so the budget resets on a new human message but not on system-kind messages.

Because a fired wakeup cron's row is never deleted by firing, schedule_thread_wakeup opportunistically purges expired thread_wakeup crons (matched conservatively on kind plus a past end_time) before creating a new one.

The baby-sit skill instructs cloud runs to use the durable manage_baby_sit watch (webhook plus 10-minute token-free fallback) while local/desktop runs instead use a bounded foreground `gh pr checks --watch` loop and never call manage_baby_sit or schedule_thread_wakeup.

Agent-usage cost refresh uses the scheduler's `agent_cost` task to fetch a run-only LangSmith cost and persist it to the invocation usage record; failed lookup or persistence advances through the same fixed five-delay retry budget and then terminates.

The purge_wakeup_crons operational script supports a dry run and deletion mode for expired `thread_wakeup` crons, resolving the deployment URL from `--url` or `LANGGRAPH_URL` and credentials from `LANGGRAPH_API_KEY` or `LANGSMITH_API_KEY`.

The `thread_feedback` scheduler task uses a stored feedback record and a thread lock to skip stale work, reschedule until a quiet period is due, and post a Slack feedback prompt only for the current ready record.
Completion telemetry records terminal agent invocation usage and schedules agent-cost enrichment only when the invocation was recorded or still needs a cost refresh.

The background-task monitor uses a second locked recheck before deleting monitor crons, preventing it from removing monitoring while a concurrent task transition reveals running or undelivered terminal work.
